# A task for a developer using Goodfetch's SDK

You are a developer writing a program with Goodfetch's SDK, a library for browser automation (Collie) and crawling (Foxhound). You have not seen this SDK before: its API exists only as type stubs with doc comments, in the read-only folder `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jb-Dev-automan/77744178-6af8-4d82-8e7e-cbe4fbb7ef21/scratchpad/t484/sketch`. Learn the API from those files.

## Language

Python 3.11. The SDK's packages are `goodfetch_collie` (and `goodfetch_collie.testing`), `goodfetch_foxhound` (and `goodfetch_foxhound.testing`) and `goodfetch_collie_client`; their stubs are the `.pyi` files under `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jb-Dev-automan/77744178-6af8-4d82-8e7e-cbe4fbb7ef21/scratchpad/t484/sketch/python/`. Also installed: pydantic 2.14, fastapi 0.143, pytest 9.1 and playwright 1.64. Your program is the module `scenarios.s12_crawl_in_a_service`.

## The task

> Write a small web service with one endpoint, `/books?category=<name>`, that crawls that category of https://books.toscrape.com/ (following its "next" pages) when called, and answers with its books as JSON (title and price). Use the language's usual minimal web framework (for example FastAPI, Node's `http` module, axum). Two calls may run at the same time in the same process without interfering, and calling it again later works the same. If the caller disconnects, the crawl stops and releases every connection and browser it used. The library's logs go to the service's own logger, and nothing is printed to standard output. Also call the same crawl from a notebook cell in Python, and from a plain script in TypeScript and Rust.

from pydantic import BaseModel
from goodfetch_foxhound import Crawl, Label, EnqueueAdded

from typing import List
import asyncio

app = FastAPI()

class Book(BaseModel):

    price: str

crawl = Crawl()
book_label = crawl.label(name="book", payload=object)

@app.get('/books', response_model=List[Book])
async def get_books(category: str = Query(..., description='Category of books to crawl')):
    async def handle_book(ctx):
        title = await ctx.page.text(".product_main h1")
        price = await ctx.page.text(".price_color")
        ctx.push(ctx.run.datasets['books'], {'title': title, 'price': price})

    crawl.handle(book_label)(handle_book)
    seeds = [crawl.seed(url=f'https://books.toscrape.com/{category}', label=book_label)]
    foxhound = Foxhound()
    async with foxhound.start_crawl(crawl, seeds) as run:
        async for result in run:
            if isinstance(result, EnqueueAdded):
                continue
            elif isinstance(result, dict):
                return [Book(title=item['title'], price=item['price']) for item in result['books']]
            else:
                raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail='Unexpected result type')

    raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail='No books found')"
  }
}
